narrative.northStar: One selected cabinet, six ways in.
narrative.overview: Arcade Marquee is the portfolio archive staged as a dark aisle of project cabinets. Its own cyan, magenta, and amber wayfinding, self-hosted Barlow typography, and ruled hardware are local to this route; the generated archive and honest project disclosures remain shared. A visitor selects one real record, sees its true preview or media, and follows the real opening path. The local People, compiled prototype is visibly bounded as fictional data. Public destinations are links, not external embeds.
keyCharacteristics: The marquee sign and square cabinet frame build physical hardware from tonal blocks, double rules, and discrete lights instead of neon glow.
One semantic project list selects one cabinet; source titles, summaries, context, artifacts, and disclosures come from the shared archive.
Attract rotation is optional and pauses for user intent, hidden/offscreen state, and reduced-motion preference.

rules.name: The Aisle Contrast Rule
rules.body: Cyan marks selection, magenta is secondary archive wayfinding, and amber indicates action or publication boundary; none of the accents encode fictional metrics.

rules.name: The Named Work Rule
rules.body: Source project titles remain visible in the semantic list and follow their own summary, context, media, publication note, and opening path.

rules.name: The Artifact Boundary Rule
rules.body: Keep every catalog disclosure beside its artifact; only the verified local demo is embedded, with a restricted sandbox.

dos: Use data/projects.json as the sole source for titles, descriptions, paths, and publication notes.
Keep all projects findable without JavaScript and retain the semantic index, visible keyboard focus, browser history, and reduced-motion support.
Place the true preview or media at the center of each selected cabinet and keep a direct opening path distinct from its preview.
donts: Do not reproduce the approved comp's invented project labels, dashboard metrics, or visualized facts.
Do not present fictional prototype data as people evidence, a live service, client outcomes, or a connected system.
Do not embed an external public site or invent an image for a link-only record.
Do not make this palette a shared default for other independently designed worlds.
